               <ns0:head>CHAP. IV.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 FOrasmuch then <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Apostle having in the former Chapter exhorted Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lievers to patient bearing of Afflictions by the Example of Christ, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18. proceeds in this to perswade them to improve the Crosses they bore outwardly to inward Mortification. Christ's Death is proposed to us in Scripture as an Exem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plar both of external Mortification in bearing Reproaches, Persecutions, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> This the Apostle prosecutes in the former Chapter, and of internal in the destroying the Body of Sin; this he exhorts to in this Chapter, and indeed draws his Ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gument from Christ's Death, not only as the exemplary, but efficient and meritorious Cause of our Mortification, and which hath a real Influence upon it, in that Christ by his Death did not only merit the Pardon of Sin, but the giving the Spirit, whereby Corruption might be destroyed, and our Natures renewed.</ns0:note> as Christ hath suffered for us <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Viz.</ns0:hi> not only as an Exemplar of Patience and Submission to the Will of God, but for the taking away of Sin, both in the Guilt and Power of it, and that he might be the Procurer as well as Pattern of our Mortifica<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:note> in the flesh <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">In his human Nature, as <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 3.18.</ns0:note>, arm your selves like<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wise with the same mind <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Strengthen, and fortifie your selves against all Temptations, and unto the Mortification of your Lusts with the Consideration of these Ends, and the mighty Efficacy of Christ's Death, he suffering in his Flesh, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> in his human Nature, that you might suffer in your Flesh, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> in your sinful corrupt Nature: Or, (which comes to the same) with the same mind which Christ had, who, in his Death, aimed not only at the Pardon of your Sin, but the Destruction of it, and the Renovation of your Natures: Or, arm your selves with the same Mind, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> a purpose of suffering in the Flesh, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> of dying spiri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ritually with Christ in the Mortification of your Flesh, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6.6, 7. as Christ died, and suffered in the Flesh, so reckon that you, by the Virtue of his Death, must die to Sin, and cruci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fie your Flesh, with its Affections and Lusts, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 5.24. or else what the same Mind is, he declares in the following clause.</ns0:note>; for <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Or rather <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word here seems rather to be ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plicative than causal.</ns0:note> he that hath suffered in the flesh <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The Old Man, his corrupt Flesh, (<ns0:hi>Flesh</ns0:hi> being taken here in a different sense from what it was in the former part of the Verse) he that is spiritually dead with Christ, whose Old Man is crucified with him.</ns0:note>, hath ceased from sin <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">From sinning willingly and delightfully, and yielding him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self up to the Power of Sin; comp. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6. which explains this: what <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> here calls <ns0:hi>suffering in the Flesh, Paul</ns0:hi> there calls a being <ns0:hi>dead to Sin,</ns0:hi> v. 2, 11. and what <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> calls a <ns0:hi>ceasing from Sin, Paul</ns0:hi> calls a <ns0:hi>living no longer in Sin,</ns0:hi> v. 2. and a being <ns0:hi>free from</ns0:hi> it, v. 7. And this may be the <ns0:hi>Mind,</ns0:hi> or Thought with which they were to be armed, that they being dead with Christ to Sin, should not live any longer in it; having their Flesh crucified, should not indulge its Affections and Lusts.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:585" />2 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 14.7.</ns0:note> That he no longer should live the rest of <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> time in the flesh <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> In the Body, meaning his natural Life. Flesh is here taken, in a third sense different from the two former; so <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 2.20. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 1.22.</ns0:note>, to the lusts of men <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">By the <ns0:hi>Lusts of Men,</ns0:hi> he means the corrupt Desires, and sinful ways of carnal Men, to which they were not to conform themselves, or make them the Rule of their living, <ns0:hi>Rom,</ns0:hi> 12.2. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.3. and <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 2.8. <ns0:hi>Tit.</ns0:hi> 1.14.</ns0:note>, but to the will of God <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The holy Will of God revealed to us in his Law, (which is the Rule by which we are to walk) in opposi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion to the Lusts of Men; we are to live not as Men would have us, but as God commands us.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 For the time past of our lives may suffice <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The Apostle doth not mean by this Expression meerly that they should forbear their former Lusts, out of a Saciety and Weariness, as having had their fill of them, but stir them up to Holiness by minding them of their former sinful life, <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> ye are concerned to run well now, when ye have for so great a part of your time run wrong.                <ns0:p n="4">4 Wherein they think it strange <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Gr. <ns0:hi>Are Strangers,</ns0:hi> i. e. carry themselves as Strangers, wondring (as at some new thing) at the change the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel hath made in you, and your no more conforming your selves to their wicked Courses; they seem to be in another World, when among you.</ns0:note>, that you run <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This seems to signifie the ea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gerness and vehemency of these Gentiles in pursuing their Lusts, and may perhaps have some respect to the Feasts of <ns0:hi>Bacchus,</ns0:hi> to which they were wont madly to run, and there commit the Abominations mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3.</ns0:note> not with them to the same excess <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>Profuse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Confusion</ns0:hi> of Riot or Luxury, and then it suites well with that heap of Sins before-mentioned, whereof this seems to be comprehensive.</ns0:note> of riot, speaking evil <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Gr. <ns0:hi>Blaspheming,</ns0:hi> or speaking evil, <ns0:hi>of you</ns0:hi> is added by the Translators: This may therefore be understood not only of their speaking evil of Believers, as void of Humanity, and Enemies to civil Society, but of God and the Christian Religion, as a dull, morose, sower way, and which they could not embrace without renouncing all Mirth and Chearfulness.</ns0:note> of <ns0:hi>you.</ns0:hi>
